creativeBrief:
Pattern: CONTRADICTION_REVEAL_V4. Audience: global English-speaking viewers; state country, model and time scope naturally. Channel angle: familiar objects with a surprising but true job. Generate five declarative, concrete subject-first hooks; prefer 6–10 words and do not give away the mechanism at once. Six story functions across five voiced scenes: visual paradox, contradiction, clue, mechanism, distinct second reveal, payoff. Target 25–29 seconds including the configured sign-off; hard max 30. Keep voice, karaoke, local BGM and channel outro. No generic spoken CTA. Visual direction: Use the photoreal live-action style in visualStyle, like varied Pexels-style footage. Open on the real object and its surprising visible detail. Build five distinct camera setups: vary at least two of shot scale, angle, location, lighting and physical action between neighboring scenes. Prefer observable actions, practical macro details, human hands, and real-world context over abstract visual metaphors. For a hidden mechanism, use a plausible exposed component or demonstration prop without pretending an invented event was filmed. Keep brand signs out if accurate rendering is doubtful. Generate a distinct Gemini still and Google Flow six-second clip per voiced scene; review action, 9:16 crop and continuity before binding local MP4s. Generated shots explain sourced facts and are not documentary proof. Packaging: make the YouTube title and description curiosity-driven, a little provocative, and specific to the subject; deliver exactly the claim the video explains. The title may tease the mechanism, but do not exaggerate risk, savings, universality or a company motive beyond the facts. The description should invite one topic-specific viewer response.
YouTube title seed: Lightning and Thunder Happen Together. So Why the Delay?
YouTube description seed: The flash arrives before the sound even though they begin in the same event. What was the longest delay you have counted? #TellMeWhyyyyyy #Shorts
Core fact: The National Weather Service says thunder is the sound generated by lightning.
Second reveal: Light reaches observers faster than sound, so the flash is seen before the thunder is heard.
Opening shot: one lightning flash and a delayed sound wave. Show it as a believable real-world shot, immediately legible in the first frame. Do not reveal the internal mechanism in the opening. Use different real camera compositions and meaningful subject motion for the clue, mechanism, second reveal and payoff. Do not use an imaginary accident, simulated rescue, or fake news-style scene. 
Fact boundaries: If thunder is audible, seek shelter; do not use a seconds count as a safety clearance.

visualStyle: Photorealistic 9:16 live-action footage with the believable look of carefully shot stock video: real objects, real locations, natural materials, practical lighting, physically plausible motion, and restrained documentary camera work. Use accurate colors, markings, geometry and scale when they carry the fact. Vary shot scale, camera angle, setting, light and movement across the five scenes; never repeat one macro view or one slow zoom five times. The subject stays recognizable, while each scene has a different visual job. No mascot, cartoon, sketch, animation graphics, floating labels, fake brand marks, surreal morphing, glossy 3D render, dark wash, or cinematic disaster spectacle. Existing words and numbers printed on real objects may be visible; do not add captions or generated text. Generated realistic footage illustrates the source-backed explanation and must not be presented as documentary evidence of an event. Subject anchor: one lightning flash and a delayed sound wave.
